exposure: sociodemographic characteristics (age, education level, number of children)
outcome: nutritional beliefs and practices during the puerperal period
avoidance of food and water postpartum
preference for Arabic coffee and peel
cohort: 381 mothers in Riyadh during their puerperal period.
finding: The study found that age, education level, number of children, and mode of delivery were associated with mothers' nutritional beliefs and practices during the puerperal period, with age predicting these beliefs and practices.
mod_finding: Mothers did not avoid food and water after normal delivery, and those who delivered naturally prioritized their dietary habits more than those with a cesarean delivery.
